concerns.text: T002 instructs fetching a PT→SOC mapping from the NLM MedDRA–SNOMED page and hard-failing if unavailable, but MedDRA hierarchy files are license-restricted and the NLM page does not expose a downloadable PT→SOC table. The task as written is likely unexecutable (guaranteed non-zero exit), and T004's ≥95% coverage gate depends on it. Specify a concrete, actually-retrievable mapping source (e.g., a named open PT→SOC table with URL, or a bundled mapping file with a documented provenance) so the implementer has a deterministic recipe.

T010 check 5 says 'proportion of flagged signals satisfying the 2-out-of-3 rule reported (SC-005, FR-005)' but names no pass condition — by construction every is_signal=True row satisfies the rule, so the check can never fail and is not a verifiable gate. Define a measurable criterion (e.g., '100% of is_signal=True rows list ≥2 signal_metrics entries, else FAIL') or drop the check.

T006 requires computing IC with 95% Wald CIs but never states the IC formula or its variance (IC = log2[(a·N)/((a+b)·(a+c))] with a specific variance estimator, per Norén et al.). 'Compute IC' plus 'Wald CI' is not self-contained for an implementer; different IC variance conventions exist. Add the formula or a cited reference implementation to make the task deterministic and the hand-checkable unit test meaningful.

T006 requires soc_cluster_stats.csv to conform to soc_cluster.schema.yaml, but that contract has additionalProperties: false while signals.csv rows carry background_rate_status; more importantly the task doesn't state which columns soc_cluster_stats.csv must contain beyond 'conforming' — the implementer must reverse-engineer from the contract. Minor: state the column set or point explicitly at the contract's required list (soc_code, soc_name, covid_count, non_covid_count, p_value, p_adj) so the deliverable is unambiguous.

T008 computes the median REPT_DATE of the combined COVID + Non-COVID cohort, while plan.md Phase 4 says the COVID-19 cohort median. The task is executable as written, but the plan/task disagreement means an implementer following the plan produces different week_offset values; align the reference cohort across artifacts (spec FR-004 says 'the cohort', so either reading is defensible — pick one).
